## Learning Objectives

1. Describe the landmark adjuvant chemoradiotherapy trials (GITSG, EORTC, ESPAC-1, RTOG 9704, EORTC 40013)
2. Trace the evolution of adjuvant chemotherapy: 5-FU → gemcitabine → GemCap → mFOLFIRINOX
3. Apply standardized resectability criteria (AHPBA/SSO/SSAT, MD Anderson, NCCN)
4. Evaluate the rationale and evidence for neoadjuvant therapy (PREOPANC, JSAP-05, ESPAC-5F, A021501)
5. Summarize standards for locally advanced and metastatic disease (FOLFIRINOX, gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel)

## Presentation Roadmap

| Section | Focus |
|---|---|
| Part 1 | Adjuvant chemoradiotherapy: GITSG → EORTC → ESPAC-1 → RTOG 9704 → RTOG-0848 |
| Part 2 | Adjuvant chemotherapy: CONKO-001, ESPAC-3/4, JASPAC-01, PRODIGE-24, APACT |
| Part 3 | Emerging adjuvant directions: vaccines, checkpoint blockade, MRD, targeted therapy |
| Part 4 | Neoadjuvant therapy: rationale, resectability criteria, PREOPANC, ongoing trials |
| Part 5 | Unresectable/metastatic disease: GemCap, FOLFIRINOX, MPACT, JCOG1407 |

## Key Abbreviations (1/2)

- **PDAC** — pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
- **EBRT** — external beam radiotherapy; **RT/CRT** — (chemo)radiotherapy
- **5-FU** — 5-fluorouracil; **FA/LV** — folinic acid/leucovorin
- **Gem** — gemcitabine; **GemCap** — gemcitabine + capecitabine
- **OS / DFS / PFS** — overall / disease-free / progression-free survival
- **HR** — hazard ratio; **CI** — confidence interval; **RR** — relative risk/response rate

## Key Abbreviations (2/2)

- **R0 / R1** — margin-negative / margin-positive resection
- **SMV, PV, SMA, CA, CHA, GDA, IVC** — vascular anatomy (superior mesenteric vein/artery, portal vein, celiac axis, common hepatic artery, gastroduodenal artery, inferior vena cava)
- **RECIST** — Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors
- **MRD** — minimal residual disease; **ctDNA** — circulating tumor DNA
- **PS** — performance status (ECOG/WHO); **QoL** — quality of life

## PART 1 · Adjuvant Chemoradiotherapy

**From early radiosensitization concepts to modern practice**

- GITSG → EORTC → ESPAC-1 → RTOG 9704 → EORTC 40013 → network meta-analysis → RTOG-0848

## Origins — EBRT + 5-FU

- Early studies examined **EBRT combined with 5-FU** as a radiosensitizing agent in **advanced, unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma**
- These identified **increased median survival over radiotherapy alone**
- This experience provided the rationale for testing chemoradiation **after potentially curative resection**

## GITSG (1979) — First Randomized Evidence

- Gastrointestinal Tumour Study Group: first RCT of adjuvant therapy after potentially curative pancreatic resection
- **43 patients randomized** to:
  - Chemoradiotherapy: **40 Gy EBRT + concurrent 5-FU**, then 5-FU for up to **2 years**
  - vs. **no adjuvant treatment**

## GITSG — Results

- **Median, 2-year, and 5-year survival were all increased** in the treatment group (Table 66.1)
- Established **proof of principle** for adjuvant chemoradiation in pancreatic cancer

## GITSG — Limitations

- **Slow recruitment:** only 43 of an intended **150 patients** enrolled over **8 years**
- **Poor compliance:** only **9%** completed the intended 2 years of therapy
- **Quality assurance problems:** **32%** had violations of the intended radiation therapy
- An additional **30 patients** were entered into the treatment group **without randomization**

## GITSG (1987) — Nonrandomized Extension

- 30 additional (nonrandomized) patients treated with **60 Gy EBRT + 5-FU → follow-on 5-FU**
- Median survival **18 months**; 2-year survival **46%** (Table 66.1)

## Corroborating Nonrandomized Studies

- Several subsequent studies showed **similar advantages** for adjuvant chemoradiation
- Important caveats:
  - **Nonrandomized** designs
  - **Small numbers of patients**

## EORTC Trial (Klinkenbijl et al.) — Design

- Phase III trial on behalf of the **European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC)**
- **218 patients** randomized after curative resection:
  - **114 pancreatic cancer**
  - **92 periampullary cancer**
- **40 Gy EBRT + concurrent 5-FU** vs. **no adjuvant treatment**

## EORTC — Results in Pancreatic Cancer

- **Non-statistically significant trend** toward survival benefit:
  - Observation: median **1.0 year** (95% CI, 0.8–1.4)
  - Treatment: median **1.3 years** (95% CI, 1.1–1.8)
  - **P = .099**
- A similar trend was noted in the **overall study population**

## EORTC — Interpretation & Caveats

- **~20% of patients randomized to chemoradiotherapy never received the intended treatment**
- Raises the question: would the benefit have been **significant if the study were adequately powered**?

## Setting the Stage — ESPAC

- The early GITSG/EORTC studies motivated the **European Study Group for Pancreatic Cancer (ESPAC)** to conduct a definitive RCT of **adjuvant chemotherapy and chemoradiotherapy** after pancreatic cancer resection

## ESPAC-1 — Design

- ~Half of patients randomized to:
  - **Chemotherapy** (bolus 5-FU × 6 months) vs. no chemotherapy, **and**
  - **Chemoradiotherapy** (20 Gy + concurrent 5-FU) vs. no chemoradiotherapy
- Other half: novel **2 × 2 factorial design**:

```text
        Randomization (2 x 2 factorial)
                     |
     +--------+--------+--------+--------+
     |        |        |        |        |
  Chemo     CRT     Both    Observation
  (5-FU x   (20 Gy+           (no
   6 mo)     5-FU)          treatment)
```

## ESPAC-1 — Scale & Uniqueness

- **541 patients** from **61 centers** in **11 countries**
- **Largest adjuvant therapy trial** in pancreatic cancer at the time
- **289 patients** in the 2 × 2 factorial design
- **256 patients** randomized to chemotherapy or chemoradiation vs. observation outside the original design (**ESPAC-1 plus**)

## ESPAC-1 — Headline Results

- Overall study: **failed to demonstrate a survival benefit for chemoradiotherapy** over observation
- **Statistically significant survival benefit for chemotherapy**
- Findings **maintained** when only the 2 × 2 factorial data were evaluated

## Table 66.2 — ESPAC-1 Data (1/2)

| Analysis | Arm | Median Survival (mo) | 2-Year (%) | 5-Year (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 × 2 chemoradiotherapy analysis | Chemoradiotherapy | 15.9 | 28.5 | 10 |
| | No chemoradiotherapy | 17.9 | 41.4 | 19.6 (P = .053) |
| 2 × 2 chemotherapy analysis | Chemotherapy | 20.1 | 39.7 | 21.1 |
| | No chemotherapy | 15.5 | 30 | 8.4 (P = .009) |

## Table 66.2 — ESPAC-1 Data (2/2): Full Factorial

| Arm (2 × 2 factorial design) | Median Survival (mo) | 2-Year (%) | 5-Year (%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Observation | 16.9 | 38.7 | 10.7 |
| Chemoradiotherapy | 13.9 | 21.7 | 7.3 |
| Chemotherapy | 21.6 | 44 | 29 (P = .0005) |
| Chemoradiotherapy + follow-on chemotherapy | 19.9 | 35 | 13.2 |

## ESPAC-1 — Criticisms

- The **2 × 2 design itself** has been criticized
- **Variation in the amount of radiotherapy received**
- **Lack of adjuvant chemotherapy in the radiation arm**
- These raised doubts about the observed **lack of benefit of radiotherapy**

## ESPAC-1 — Why the Data Remain Relevant

- Data from **both patient sets** are relevant
- Chemotherapy benefit evident in **both R1 (margin-positive)** and **R0 (margin-negative)** patients
- The 2 × 2 design answered the two most important questions:
  1. Is there a benefit for **adjuvant chemoradiotherapy**?
  2. Is there a benefit for **adjuvant chemotherapy**?

## Meta-analytic Confirmation

- Meta-analyses confirmed the survival advantage of adjuvant chemotherapy:
  - **Reduced risk of death: 25%** (95% CI, 0.64–0.90; **P = .001**)
- Benefit **more pronounced in R0** vs. R1 margin patients
- Survival advantage **maintained when adjusted for quality of life** over the 24 months after resection
- **Conclusion:** chemotherapy — not radiotherapy — provides the significant survival impact in resected pancreatic cancer

## RTOG 9704 — Question & Design

- Evaluated **gemcitabine** in conjunction with adjuvant chemoradiotherapy
- **451 patients**, stratified by **tumor size, nodal involvement, resection margin status**

```text
Randomize
   |
   +-- Arm A: Gem x 3 wk -> 50.4 Gy EBRT + infusional 5-FU -> Gem x 10-12 wk
   |
   +-- Arm B: 5-FU x 3 wk -> 50.4 Gy EBRT + infusional 5-FU -> 5-FU x 10-12 wk
```

## RTOG 9704 — Results

- Median survival **not improved** with gemcitabine:
  - Gemcitabine: **20.5 months**
  - 5-FU: **16.9 months**
  - **HR = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.67–1.05; P = .12**
- 5-year analysis: **no changes to the original inferences**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| EORTC-40013 | 45 | 4 cycles of Gem | 24.4 | 50.2 | — |
| | 45 | 2 cycles of Gem → Gem + 50.5 Gy EBRT | 24.3 | 50.6 | — |
| RTOG-9704 (head of pancreas only; eligible n = 388) | 187 | Gem pre-CRT, 50.4 Gy EBRT + 5-FU, Gem post-CRT | 20.5^a^ | — | 31 |

^a^HR 0.82; CI 0.65–1.03; P = .09. *CRT, chemoradiotherapy; Gem, gemcitabine.*

## EORTC 40013/FFCD/GERCOR — Design

- Rationale: ESPAC-1 showed chemotherapy benefit — **could chemoradiotherapy improve on it?**
- **Phase II** trial; **90 patients**, **R0 resections only**
- Arm A: chemotherapy alone — **4 cycles gemcitabine**
- Arm B: **2 courses gemcitabine → 50.4 Gy EBRT + weekly gemcitabine × 5–6 weeks**

## EORTC 40013 — Results

- **Primary endpoint (toxicity): comparable** in both arms
- **Overall survival: 24 months in both arms**
- **Disease-free survival:** 12 months (CRT arm) vs. 11 months (chemo-alone arm)
- **Local relapse:** lower with CRT — **11% vs. 24%**
- **Distant metastases:** no difference — **42% vs. 40%**

## EORTC 40013 — Interpretation

- Chemoradiotherapy added to chemotherapy can **reduce the incidence of local recurrence**, even though it does **not demonstrate an overall survival benefit**

## PEFG Induction — Intensification Fails

- Phase II RCT: does **more intense chemotherapy before chemoradiotherapy** help?
- **3 months induction PEFG** (cisplatin, epirubicin, 5-FU, gemcitabine) **vs. gemcitabine**
- Followed by chemoradiotherapy: **54–60 Gy RT + infusional 5-FU**
- Result: intensification **did not increase survival**

## Network Meta-analysis — Quantifying Benefit

- Systematic review + network meta-analysis: **9 high-quality studies, 3033 patients**
- Randomized across **6 treatment arms** (chemotherapy and/or chemoradiotherapy)
- **Adjuvant chemotherapy with 5-FU or gemcitabine reduces mortality by at least one-third** in resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma
- **Unclear** whether chemoradiation + chemotherapy is more effective than chemotherapy alone for survival
- **Radiotherapy added toxicity**

## Geographic Practice Divide

- **North America:** adjuvant chemoradiation continues in many parts (contrast with Europe/Asia, where **adjuvant chemotherapy is standard of care**)
- North American guidelines favor adjuvant chemotherapy **while allowing the addition of chemoradiotherapy**, particularly in **high-risk recurrence settings** (e.g., positive resection margins)

## Interferon-Based Adjuvant Protocols

- Evaluated in the adjuvant setting
- **No improvement in survival**
- **Significant toxicity**

## NRG/RTOG-0848 — Design

- Joint NRG (National Radiation Group)/RTOG-0848 **Phase III** trial (NCT01013649); commenced **2009**
- Target: **950 patients** with resected pancreatic head cancer
- **Step 1:** adjuvant **gemcitabine vs. gemcitabine + erlotinib**
- **Step 2** (after 5 cycles gemcitabine, no progression): **fluoropyrimidine + radiotherapy vs. continued gemcitabine-based chemotherapy**

## RTOG-0848 — Erlotinib Randomization Results

- **163 gemcitabine** vs. **159 gemcitabine + erlotinib**
- Median follow-up: **42.5 months** (surviving patients)
- Median OS: **29.9 months** (gem; 95% CI, 21.7–33.4) vs. **28.1 months** (gem + erlotinib; 95% CI, 20.7–30.9)
- **HR 1.04; P = .062** — no benefit with erlotinib
- Design modified to **gemcitabine-based combinations**; radiation randomization completed — **final results anticipated 2022**

## PART 2 · Adjuvant Chemotherapy

**From biomodulated 5-FU to mFOLFIRINOX**

- ESPAC-1 → CONKO-001 → ESPAC-3 → JASPAC-01 → ESPAC-4 → PRODIGE-24 → APACT

## Foundation — ESPAC-1 & Meta-analyses

- ESPAC-1 provided the **first evidence of survival benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy** (biomodulated 5-FU regimens)
- Benefit evident in **both R1 and R0 resections**
- Two meta-analyses confirmed:
  - **25% reduced mortality risk** (95% CI, 0.64–0.90; P = .001)
  - Advantage in **R0 vs. R1** margin patients
- Survival advantage **maintained when adjusted for QoL** during 24 months post-resection
- This advance drove the **next generation of trials**: ESPAC-3 (version 2), ESPAC-4, and translational runoffs

## Emergence of Gemcitabine

- Emerging evidence in the **1990s** demonstrated gemcitabine's value, initially in **advanced disease**
- Provided the platform for adjuvant testing

## CONKO-001 — Design

- **Multicenter Phase III RCT**
- **Adjuvant gemcitabine vs. observation** after resection of pancreatic cancer

## CONKO-001 — Disease-Free Survival

- Median DFS: **13.4 months** (95% CI, 11.4–15.3) with gemcitabine vs. **6.9 months** (95% CI, 6.1–7.8) with observation
- **P < .001**
- DFS: **3-year 23.5% vs. 7.5%**; **5-year 16.5% vs. 5.5%** (gemcitabine vs. observation)

## CONKO-001 — Overall Survival

- Median OS: **22.1 months** (95% CI, 18.4–25.8) vs. **20.2 months** (95% CI, 17–23.4)
- **P = .06** — not statistically significant
- OS: **3-year 34% vs. 20.5%**; **5-year 22.5% vs. 11.5%**

## CONKO-001 — Long-Term Follow-up

- 5- and 10-year analyses continued to demonstrate **significantly improved OS**:
  - **5-year: 20.7% vs. 10.4%**
  - **10-year: 12.2% vs. 7.7%** (gemcitabine vs. observation)
- Establishes a **durable survival advantage** for adjuvant gemcitabine

## Yoshitomi et al. — Gem ± UFT

- Gemcitabine vs. gemcitabine + uracil/tegafur (UFT)
- Median OS: **29.8 vs. 21.2 months** (P = .28)
- **Addition of fluoropyrimidine to gemcitabine did not improve survival**
- Both smaller studies provided **similar survival estimates** for gemcitabine with a benefit over observation

## JSAP-02 — Gemcitabine vs Surgery Alone

- Gemcitabine vs. surgery alone
- Median OS: **22.3 vs. 18.4 months** (HR 0.77; 95% CI, 0.51–1.14; P = .19)
- **5-year survival: 23.9% vs. 10.6%**

## The Unanswered Question → ESPAC-3

- CONKO-001: gemcitabine > observation ✓
- Yoshitomi: gem + fluoropyrimidine not > gemcitabine ✓
- **Remaining question: is gemcitabine superior to 5-FU** in the adjuvant setting?
- → **ESPAC-3** set out to answer this

## ESPAC-3 — Design & Results

- **1088 patients** with PDAC
- **5-FU/leucovorin (folinic acid)** vs. **gemcitabine**
- **No difference** in:
  - OS by treatment (**P = .39**)
  - Treatment effect by resection status (**P = .56**)
  - Progression-free survival (**P = .44**)
- Median OS: **23.6 vs. 23.0 months** (gem vs. 5-FU/FA)

## ESPAC-3 — Why Gemcitabine Won

- **Similar efficacy** to 5-FU/FA
- **Significantly reduced side effect and toxicity profile**
- → Gemcitabine became the preferred adjuvant platform

## ESPAC-3 — Timing & Duration (Valle et al.)

- **Completion of all 6 cycles** of adjuvant chemotherapy was an **independent prognostic factor** after resection
- **No survival disadvantage** from delaying chemotherapy initiation **up to 12 weeks** after resection
- In the subgroup completing < 6 months: those starting **after 8 weeks fared better** than those starting before 8 weeks
- Suggests benefit to **delaying chemotherapy up to 12 weeks** to allow adequate postoperative recovery
- **Caution:** interpretation of non-prespecified subgroup analyses

## JASPAC-01 — Design & S-1

- **Phase III, multi-institutional trial, Japan**; **385 patients**: gemcitabine vs. **S-1** (orally active fluoropyrimidine)
- **S-1 composition:**
  - **Tegafur** — prodrug of 5-FU
  - **Gimeracil** — minimizes systemic toxicity (inhibits 5-FU degradation)
  - **Oteracil** — minimizes gastrointestinal toxicity
  - Net effect: **increases the tolerable tumor dose of 5-FU**
- S-1 was **noninferior to gemcitabine in advanced disease** → adjuvant noninferiority tested here

## JASPAC-01 — Results

- **Stopped early** at interim analysis per prespecified discontinuation criteria; all protocol treatments completed
- **5-year OS: 44.1% (S-1) vs. 24.4% (gemcitabine)** (table reports 24.2%)
- **Median OS (per protocol): 46.5 vs. 25.5 months**; HR 0.57
- **3-year OS: 59.7% vs. 38.8%** (P < .0001 per protocol)
- S-1 determined **noninferior** (indeed superior) to gemcitabine in Japanese patients

## JASPAC-01 — Generalizability Caveat

- **S-1 is not approved in the West**
- Uncertain how generalizable these findings are **outside of Japan**

## Multi-agent Attempts — Bakkevold (FAM)

- Patients after pancreatic resection (**61 radical resections**, including 14 periampullary cancers)
- **FAM** (5-FU + doxorubicin/Adriamycin + mitomycin C) vs. observation
- **Median survival: 23 vs. 11 months (P = .02)** — significant
- **But:** no improvement in **3-year or 5-year** survival
- **Increased toxicity**; only **56%** completed the six courses

## Takada et al. — MMC + 5-FU

- **508 patients** with mixed pancreaticobiliary cancers (**158 pancreatic cancer**)
- Surgery alone vs. surgery + **mitomycin C + 5-FU**
- 5-year survival **not significantly different: 11.5% vs. 18%**
- Key caveat: used **oral 5-FU** — lower bioavailability than IV due to **first-pass hepatic metabolism**

## Kosuge et al. — Cisplatin + 5-FU

- Multicenter RCT: surgery vs. surgery + **cisplatin + 5-FU**
- **60% of patients also received 30 Gy intraoperative radiotherapy**
- Conclusion: safe and well tolerated, but **no survival benefit**
- Median OS 12.5 vs. 15.8 months; 5-year 26.4% vs. 14.9% (P = .94)

## GemCap — From Advanced Disease to Adjuvant Testing

- Gemcitabine + **capecitabine** (orally active 5-FU prodrug)
- Produced a **small improvement in survival vs. gemcitabine alone in advanced disease**
- Rationale for adjuvant evaluation in **ESPAC-4**

## ESPAC-4 — Design

- **732 patients** after curative resection for PDAC
- Randomized:
  - **Gemcitabine (n = 366)**
  - **GemCap (n = 364)**

## ESPAC-4 — Results

- Median OS: **28.0 months GemCap** (95% CI, 23.5–31.5) vs. **25.5 months gemcitabine** (95% CI, 22.7–27.9)
- **HR = 0.82 (95% CI, 0.68–0.98); P = .032**

## ESPAC-4 — Updated Analysis & Clinical Role

- Updated analysis maintained benefit:
  - Median OS **30.2 months** (95% CI, 25.8–33.5) vs. **27.9 months** (95% CI, 24.8–29.9)
- **GemCap established as an adjuvant option**
- Now typically used for **older patients** and/or patients with **ECOG performance status > 1**

## PRODIGE-24/ACCORD-24/CCTG PA.6 — Design

- Established **adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX** (5-FU, oxaliplatin, leucovorin, irinotecan) as standard for **fit patients** after curative surgery
- **493 patients** randomized: adjuvant **mFOLFIRINOX vs. gemcitabine** × 6 months

## PRODIGE-24 — Eligibility

- **WHO performance status 0–1**
- **CA19-9 < 180 U/mL**
- **R0 or R1 resection**

## PRODIGE-24 — Results

- Median follow-up: **33.6 months** (surviving patients)
- **Median DFS: 21.6 vs. 12.8 months** — HR 0.58 (95% CI, 0.46–0.73); **P < .001**
- **Median OS: 54.4 vs. 35.0 months** — HR 0.64 (95% CI, 0.48–0.86); **P = .03**

## PRODIGE-24 — Toxicity & Practice Impact

- **Grade 3–4 adverse events: 75.9% (mFOLFIRINOX) vs. 52.9% (gemcitabine)**
- These data **immediately changed practice**
- Support recommendation of **adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX for good performance status patients**

## APACT — Design

- **Adjuvant PAnCreas Trial** — role of **gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel** in the adjuvant setting
- **866 patients**: gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel vs. gemcitabine alone × 6 cycles
- Eligibility similar to adjuvant PRODIGE trial
- Primary endpoint: **DFS adjudicated by blinded independent central review**

## APACT — Results

- Median follow-up: **38.5 months**
- **DFS: 19.5 vs. 18.8 months** — HR 0.88 (95% CI, 0.729–1.063); **P = .18** (not significant; table: 19.4 months)
- **Interim median OS: 40.5 vs. 36.2 months** — HR 0.82 (95% CI, 0.68–0.99); **P = .045**

## APACT — Current Status

- **Mature OS data awaited** — interim analysis did not show significant benefit with the doublet for the primary endpoint
- Gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel **remains investigational** in the adjuvant setting

## Moving the Adjuvant Benchmark

Key factors improving adjuvant therapy outcomes:

- **Improved patient selection** (e.g., limiting by CA19-9 level)
- **Integration of optimal supportive therapy measures**
- **Improvements in therapy**

## PART 3 · Emerging Directions in Adjuvant Therapy

**Recruiting the immune system and targeting tumor biology**

- Vaccines · Checkpoint blockade · MRD-guided therapy · Germline-targeted agents

## Immunotherapy — The New Frontier

- A preponderance of **ongoing adjuvant trials attempt to recruit the immune system**
- Primarily in the form of **vaccines and checkpoint blockade**, given **after completion of standard adjuvant regimens**

## MSK Personalized RNA Vaccine (NCT04161755)

- Pilot **nonrandomized** study — Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center
- Combines:
  - **RO7198457** — personalized RNA-based cancer vaccine
  - **Atezolizumab** — PD-L1 antibody
  - **Chemotherapy**
- Vaccine uses **tumor antigens obtained from the surgical specimen** — unique to each individual patient's cancer

## KRAS Vaccine Approaches

- **Johns Hopkins (NCT04117087):** KRAS vaccine + **dual checkpoint blockade** — nivolumab (anti-PD-1) + ipilimumab (anti-CTLA4)
- **University of Pennsylvania (NCT03592888):** KRAS vaccine after **depletion of regulatory T-cells with cyclophosphamide**
- **NCT01088789 (Phase II):** allogeneic pancreatic tumor cell vaccine + cyclophosphamide

## MRD-Guided Therapy & AMPLIFY

- Emerging direction: incorporation of **minimal residual disease (MRD) status** into treatment decisions
- **AMPLIFY trial:** patients with **KRAS-mutated disease** and **MRD detected via circulating tumor DNA** are treated with **KRAS-targeted immunotherapy**
- **ELI-002:** mutant KRAS peptides + immune stimulant

## APOLLO (NCT04858334)

- **Phase II RCT** in resected pancreatic cancer
- Investigates a **targeted drug (olaparib, PARP inhibitor)** in patients with germline mutations in **BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2** + chemotherapy vs. placebo + chemotherapy

## PART 4 · Neoadjuvant Treatment of Pancreatic Cancer

**Treating earlier: rationale, resectability, and evidence**

- Rationale → meta-analysis → resectability criteria → PREOPANC → JSAP-05 → TNT → ongoing phase III trials

## Why Neoadjuvant? — The R1 Problem

- Neoadjuvant treatment is **increasingly incorporated** into management of localized pancreatic cancer
- Even patients deemed to have **resectable disease**: a large number have **microscopically incomplete (R1) resections** after surgery

## Computational Rationale

- Mathematical and computational analysis of primary pancreatic tumors and metastases:
  - Pancreatic tumors grow in an **exponential manner**
  - Patients are **likely to have metastases at diagnosis**
- Modeling suggested: **targeting tumor cells while they are rapidly growing is crucial** — **any delay in treatment may be detrimental**

## Goals of Neoadjuvant Therapy

- **Increase the number of patients with resectable disease**
- **Treat micrometastases not evident at staging**

## Limitations of Existing Evidence

- Proposed **> 30 years ago**; benefit demonstrated in some other tumor types
- **Limited phase III RCT data** in pancreatic cancer
- Many prior trials suffered **poor recruitment and closed early**
- Many **grouped locally advanced with borderline resectable cancers**
- Ongoing debate: **most appropriate patient groups, optimal regimen, definition of borderline disease**

## Phase II RCT — Gem/Cisplatin Neoadjuvant CRT

- Neoadjuvant chemoradiation (**gemcitabine + cisplatin**) followed by surgery vs. **immediate surgery** in resectable pancreatic cancer
- Required **254 patients** — **terminated early** due to slow recruitment (**33 eligible patients per arm**)

- Results:
  - Tumor resection: **23 vs. 19 patients**
  - **R0 resection: 48% vs. 52%**
  - **pN0 rate: 30% vs. 39%**
  - Postoperative complications: **comparable**
  - **Median OS: 14.4 vs. 17.4 months**

## Gillen Meta-analysis — Design

- **111 studies** reviewed (**56 phase I/II**); median **31 patients/study** (IQR, 19–46)
- Compared treatment of:
  - **Group 1:** resectable tumors
  - **Group 2:** nonresectable (borderline resectable/unresectable) tumors

## Gillen — Treatment Landscape

- Neoadjuvant **chemotherapy**: **96.4%** received gemcitabine, fluoropyrimidines, mitomycin C, and platinum compounds
- Neoadjuvant **radiotherapy**: **93.7%** received doses ranging **24–63 Gy**

## Gillen — Resectability & Response

- Resectability estimated at **73.6% (Group 1)** vs. **33.2% (Group 2)**
- Group 2 had **higher resection-associated morbidity and mortality**
- **Combination chemotherapy** → higher estimated response and resection probabilities in initially unresectable disease vs. monotherapy

## Gillen — Survival After Resection

- Median survival after resection:
  - **Group 1: 23.3 months** (range, 12–54)
  - **Group 2: 20.5 months** (range, 9–62)

## Implications — Resectable Disease

- Data argue there is **no advantage to neoadjuvant treatment in resectable disease** vs. current practice of **resection + adjuvant therapy**
- Recognizing that apparent early-stage pancreatic cancer can metastasize frequently:
- Current guidance: neoadjuvant therapy in resectable disease is **optimally evaluated in clinical trials** or when **poor prognostic factors** are evident

## Poor Prognostic Factors Favoring Neoadjuvant Use

- **Elevated CA19-9**
- **Large primary tumors**
- **Large regional lymph nodes**
- **Equivocal extrapancreatic imaging lesions**
- **Excessive weight loss**
- **Extreme pain**

## Implications — Locally Advanced/Unresectable

- **20%–30%** of patients initially staged as locally advanced/unresectable may undergo **resection after neoadjuvant treatment**
- With **survival rates comparable to resectable cases**

## Evolution of Neoadjuvant Philosophy

- **Historical concept:** neoadjuvant treatment to **avoid surgery in poor responders** (aggressive tumor biology)
- **Modern thinking:** neoadjuvant treatment may **improve survival of patients who respond**
- → Findings suggest a need for trials focusing on **borderline/unresectable disease**

## Defining Resectability — Consensus Process

- Crucial point in evaluating neoadjuvant therapy: **criteria for defining resectability**
- **Multi-institutional, multidisciplinary team of experts**: radiologists, gastroenterologists, hepatobiliary surgeons formulated a **consensus statement**

## Resectable Disease — Criteria

Per the preoperative reporting template:

1. **No evidence of SMV or portal vein (PV) distortion**
2. **Clear fat planes** around the **celiac axis (CA)**, **hepatic artery (HA)**, and **superior mesenteric artery (SMA)**

## Borderline Resectable — Criteria

1. **Venous involvement of SMV/PV** with distortion, narrowing, or occlusion of the vein — yet allowing **safe resection and replacement**
2. **Gastroduodenal artery encasement up to the HA** with either short-segment encasement or direct abutment of the HA, **without extension to the CA**
3. **Tumor abutment of the SMA ≤ 180 degrees** of the vessel wall circumference

## Unresectable — Criteria

1. **Unreconstructable SMV or PV occlusion**; arterial involvement depends on tumor location:
2. **Pancreatic head tumor:** > 180° **SMA encasement**, **any CA abutment**, or **IVC** involvement
3. **Pancreatic body/tail tumor:** **SMA or CA encasement > 180°**

## Table 66.7 — AHPBA/SSO/SSAT Classification

| Localization | Potentially Resectable | Borderline Resectable | Locally Advanced |
|---|---|---|---|
| SMV/PV | No abutment or encasement | Abutment, encasement, or occlusion | Not constructible |
| SMA | No abutment or encasement | Abutment | Encasement |
| CHA | No abutment or encasement | Abutment or short-segment encasement | Long-segment encasement |
| Celiac trunk | No abutment or encasement | No abutment or encasement | Abutment |

*Abutment, < 180 degrees of vascular circumference; encasement, ≥ 180 degrees.*

## Table 66.7 — MD Anderson Classification

| Localization | Potentially Resectable | Borderline Resectable | Locally Advanced |
|---|---|---|---|
| SMV/PV | Abutment or encasement without occlusion | Short-segment occlusion | Not constructible |
| SMA | No abutment or encasement | Abutment | Encasement |
| CHA | No abutment or encasement | Abutment or short-segment encasement | Long-segment encasement |
| Celiac trunk | No abutment or encasement | Abutment | Encasement |

## Two Classifications, Subtle Differences

- Two main North American classifications:
  - **MD Anderson Classification**
  - **AHPBA/SSO/SSAT consensus guidelines** (American Hepato-Pancreato-Biliary Association/Society of Surgical Oncology/Society for Surgery of the Alimentary Tract)
- Both define: **potentially resectable**, **borderline resectable**, and **locally unresectable** disease
- Most definitions **overlap**, with a few **differences**

## NCCN Guidelines & International Endorsement

- These classifications + the **radiology reporting template** (Al-Hawary et al.) form the most recent **NCCN guidelines** (Table 66.8)
- Largely endorsed by the **International Study Group for Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS)**

## Table 66.8 — NCCN (v2.2021) Resectability Criteria: Venous (1/2)

| Status | Criteria |
|---|---|
| Resectable | No radiographic evidence of tumor contact with SMV or PV, **or** ≤ 180° contact **without vein distortion** |
| Borderline resectable | Solid tumor contact with SMV/PV **> 180°**; or contact ≤ 180° **with distortion or thrombosis** but with suitable vessel proximal and distal allowing complete resection with **vein reconstruction**; solid tumor contact with **IVC** |
| Locally advanced | **Unreconstructable** SMV or PV because of tumor involvement or occlusion |

## Table 66.8 — NCCN (v2.2021) Resectability Criteria: Arterial (2/2)

| Site | Resectable | Borderline Resectable | Locally Advanced |
|---|---|---|---|
| Head/uncinate | No arterial tumor contact involving CA, SMA, or CHA | CHA contact without extension to CA or hepatic artery bifurcation (resectable/reconstructable); SMA contact ≤ 180°; contact with variant arterial anatomy | SMA contact > 180°; CA contact > 180° |
| Body/tail | CA contact ≤ 180° | SMA or CA contact > 180°; CA contact > 180° without aortic involvement and with intact, uninvolved GDA permitting **modified Appleby** | CA contact **with aortic involvement** |

## MD Anderson — Borderline Disease Review

- Review of **129 patients with borderline disease** from MD Anderson Cancer Center
- Identified **considerable discrepancies** in classification of potentially resectable, borderline resectable, and locally unresectable disease **between the MD Anderson and AHPBA/SSO/SSAT systems**

## MD Anderson — Response to Neoadjuvant Therapy

- **122 patients restaged** after neoadjuvant therapy (RECIST v1.1):
  - **84 (69%) stable disease**
  - **15 (12%) partial response**
  - **23 (19%) progressive disease**
- **Only 1 patient (0.8%) had radiographic downstaging**
- Yet **85 patients (66%) underwent pancreatectomy**

## RECIST — A Poor Yardstick (and Survival Data)

- Median survival: **22 months** (all 129 patients); **33 months** for those who underwent resection
- **Current consensus:** RECIST criteria **cannot accurately determine tumor response and efficacy of neoadjuvant therapy**

## PREOPANC — Landmark Phase III Design

- One of the **first phase III RCTs of neoadjuvant vs. adjuvant therapy** reported in pancreatic cancer; updated analysis at median follow-up **56 months**
- **246 patients** (resectable + borderline) randomized:

```text
Arm 1: Surgery -> adjuvant gemcitabine (n = 127)
Arm 2: Gemcitabine -> gemcitabine + RT -> surgery
       -> adjuvant gemcitabine (n = 119)
```

## PREOPANC — Results

- **R0 resection rate: 72% vs. 43% (P < .001)** favoring the neoadjuvant group
- **Median OS (intent-to-treat): 15.7 vs. 14.3 months** — HR 0.73 (95% CI, 0.56–0.96); **P = .025**
- Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy also associated with:
  - **Improved disease-free survival**
  - **Lower lymph node involvement** at resection
  - **Less neurovascular invasion**

## PREOPANC — Resected Subset

- For patients who underwent resection:
  - **Neoadjuvant: 33.7 months** vs. **initial surgery: 17.3 months**
  - **HR 0.47 (95% CI, 0.32–0.67); P = .029**
- Demonstrated benefits of neoadjuvant gemcitabine + radiotherapy over adjuvant gemcitabine alone, particularly in **patients successfully resected after neoadjuvant therapy**

## Preop-02/JSAP-05 — Japanese Evidence

- Japan; **phase II/III**; resectable or borderline resectable disease
- **6 weeks neoadjuvant gemcitabine + S-1** vs. **initial surgery**
- All resected patients received **adjuvant S-1 × 24 weeks**
- **Median OS: 36.7 vs. 26.7 months** — HR 0.72 (95% CI, 0.55–0.94); **P = .015**
- Provides **phase III evidence supporting neoadjuvant therapy in an Asian population**

## TNT (MGH) — Design

- Massachusetts General Hospital; **total neoadjuvant treatment (TNT)** strategy
- **48 patients** with **borderline resectable** pancreatic cancer
- **8 cycles FOLFIRINOX**, then:
  - **No vascular involvement → short-course radiation**
  - **Residual vascular involvement → standard 5.5-week long-course radiation**
- Radiotherapy administered **concurrently with capecitabine**

## TNT (MGH) — Results

- Entire cohort: **median PFS 14.7 months**; **median OS 37.7 months**
- **65% (32/48) underwent surgery**, with **97% R0 resection**
- Resected group: **median PFS 48.6 months**; **median OS not reached**
- Survival compares **favorably to adjuvant benchmarks (PRODIGE-24)** — calls for a **large RCT** of neoadjuvant chemo ± radiotherapy

## A021501 — Design

- **2021 preliminary results**; phase II RCT in **borderline resectable** pancreatic cancer
- Two parallel arms vs. **historical control** (not designed for direct arm comparison):
  - **mFOLFIRINOX → hypofractionated radiation**, or
  - **mFOLFIRINOX alone**
  - Both followed by surgery
- Primary endpoint: **18-month OS**

## A021501 — Results

- **Radiation arm closed early** — lack of efficacy at preplanned interim analysis
- **18-month OS: 47.3%** (radiation arm; 95% CI, 33.7–59.7) vs. **67.9%** (chemotherapy alone; 95% CI, 54.6–78.0)
- Chemotherapy arm **compared favorably to historical controls** and **met the predefined benchmark** of relative efficacy (**> 50%**)
- Conclusion: supports **neoadjuvant systemic therapy** in borderline resectable pancreatic cancer

## SWOG S1515 — Perioperative Comparison

- **Southwest Oncology Group phase II RCT** — perioperative **mFOLFIRINOX** vs. **gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel** in **resectable** pancreatic cancer
- **Primary endpoint 2-year OS: 47%** (95% CI, 31–61) mFOLFIRINOX vs. **48%** (95% CI, 31–63) gem/nab-paclitaxel
- **Median OS: 23.2** (95% CI, 17.6–45.9) vs. **23.6 months** (95% CI, 17.8–31.7)
- **Median DFS after resection: 10.9 vs. 14.2 months**
- No direct comparison allowed by design, but the **gem/nab-paclitaxel arm performed better than expected** — suggesting a larger-than-expected perioperative role

## ESPAC-5F — Design

- **Phase II RCT**; small **4-arm** study in **borderline resectable** pancreatic cancer
- **Upfront surgery followed by adjuvant GemCap** vs. **3 neoadjuvant regimens**:
  - **GemCap**
  - **FOLFIRINOX**
  - **Chemoradiation with capecitabine** as radiosensitizer
- **90 patients enrolled**

## ESPAC-5F — Results

- **Resection rate: 62% (upfront surgery) vs. 55% (combined neoadjuvant arms)** — P = .668
- **1-year survival: 40% (upfront surgery; 95% CI, 26–62) vs. 77% (neoadjuvant; 95% CI, 66–89)**
- **HR 0.27 (95% CI, 0.13–0.55); P < .001**
- Investigators concluded a **survival advantage to neoadjuvant therapy over upfront surgery**

## Ongoing Neoadjuvant Trials

- **PREOPANC-2** (Netherlands) — all-neoadjuvant approach
- **Alliance A021806** (North America) — the definitive neoadjuvant vs. adjuvant question
- **NEPAFOX** — perioperative FOLFIRINOX (closed early)

## PREOPANC-2

- Dutch Pancreatic Cancer Group — **completed enrollment** (EudraCT 2017-002036-17; NL7094)
- **All-neoadjuvant approach**; resectable or borderline resectable disease:

```text
Arm 1: Neoadjuvant mFOLFIRINOX x 8 -> surgery
Arm 2: PREOPANC regimen:
       gemcitabine -> gemcitabine/RT -> surgery
       -> adjuvant gemcitabine
```

## Alliance A021806 (NCT04340141)

- **Phase III RCT**; planned **344 patients** with **resectable** pancreatic cancer:

```text
Arm 1: Initial surgery -> adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX
Arm 2: mFOLFIRINOX x 8 (neoadjuvant) -> surgery
       -> 4 additional adjuvant cycles
```

- **Activated 2020**; currently the **only North American RCT** specifically addressing **neoadjuvant vs. adjuvant chemotherapy**

## NEPAFOX

- Randomized **phase II/III** study: **neoadjuvant/adjuvant FOLFIRINOX** vs. **surgery + adjuvant gemcitabine**
- Planned for **310 patients** — **stopped early due to slow accrual** (40 patients over 3 years)
- Findings **suggested an advantage for adjuvant gemcitabine** over perioperative FOLFIRINOX — but too **underpowered** to be more than descriptive

## PART 5 · Treatment for Unresectable Pancreatic Cancer

**Locally advanced and metastatic disease**

- 5-FU foundation → gemcitabine → combination era → FOLFIRINOX and gem/nab-paclitaxel

## Scope & 5-FU Foundation

- Unresectable pancreatic cancer encompasses:
  - **Locally advanced disease** not amenable to surgical resection
  - Disease with **de novo metastases**
- RCTs demonstrated **5-FU and 5-FU-based regimens improve survival and quality of life vs. best supportive care** in advanced disease

## Gemcitabine — New Gold Standard (Burris)

- Gemcitabine **replaced 5-FU** as gold standard for palliative therapy in the **late 1990s**
- Pivotal phase III trial demonstrated:
  - Improvement in several QoL parameters (**Clinical Benefit Response**)
  - **Modest improvement in median OS: 5.65 vs. 4.41 months** vs. bolus 5-FU (**P = .0025**)

## GemCap — Advanced Disease

- **553 patients** with advanced pancreatic cancer; gemcitabine + capecitabine vs. gemcitabine monotherapy
- **Objective response rate: 19.1% vs. 12.4% (P = .034)**
- **Improved PFS: HR 0.78 (95% CI, 0.66–0.93); P = .004**
- **Trend toward improved OS: HR 0.86 (95% CI, 0.72–1.02); P = .08**

## GemCap — Meta-analysis & Stage Subgroups

- Survival benefit **confirmed in meta-analysis**: **HR 0.86 (95% CI, 0.75–0.98); P = .020**
- GemCap became an **accepted regimen** in advanced pancreatic cancer
- Benefit applied to **both locally advanced (155 patients)** and **metastatic disease (377 patients)** — similar OS benefit by stage

## CCTG PA.3 — Gem + Erlotinib (Moore)

- NCIC CTG study: **gemcitabine-erlotinib vs. gemcitabine alone**
- **Survival benefit in the whole population** (locally advanced + metastatic): **6.24 vs. 5.91 months; P = .038**
- Benefit **less pronounced in the locally advanced group** (138 of 569 patients) — likely because of being **underpowered for subset analysis**

## PRODIGE-4/ACCORD-11 — FOLFIRINOX (Conroy)

- Phase III trial in metastatic disease
- **FOLFIRINOX** (folinic acid + 5-FU + irinotecan + oxaliplatin) vs. gemcitabine
- **Median OS: 11.1 vs. 6.8 months (P < .001)**
- **Response rate: 31.6% vs. 9.4%**

## MPACT — Gem + nab-Paclitaxel (Von Hoff)

- Phase III trial in metastatic disease
- **Gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel** vs. gemcitabine
- **Median OS: 8.5 vs. 6.7 months (P < .001)**
- **Response rate: 23% vs. 7%**

## FOLFIRINOX vs Gem/Nab-P — The Gap

- **Both regimens recommended** for metastatic disease with **good performance status and normal liver function**
- FOLFIRINOX has **not been thoroughly compared head-to-head** with gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel — **except in retrospective analyses**
- **JCOG1407**: one of the **first prospective randomized comparisons** (in locally advanced disease)

## Eligibility Differences & European Guidelines

- **MPACT allowed:** patients **> 75 years** and **ECOG PS 2** — **both excluded** from PRODIGE
- **European guidelines:** FOLFIRINOX for patients:
  - **Up to 75 years of age**
  - **ECOG performance status 0–1**
  - **Bilirubin up to 1.5 × upper limit of normal**

## JCOG1407 — Prospective Comparison in LAPC

- **Phase II RCT**; **locally advanced pancreatic cancer**; Japanese institutions; **126 patients** (62 mFOLFIRINOX vs. 64 gem/nab-paclitaxel)
- **1-year OS: 77.4%** (FOLFIRINOX; 95% CI, 64.9–86.0) vs. **82.5%** (gem/nab; 95% CI, 70.7–89.9) — initially favoring gem/nab-paclitaxel
- **2-year OS: 48.2%** (95% CI, 33.3–61.7) vs. **39.7%** (95% CI, 28.6–52.5) — direction reversed
- **Median OS: 2.0 years** (95% CI, 1.6–2.7) vs. **1.8 years** (95% CI, 1.5–2.0)
- **Significant confidence interval overlap** — await further maturity of the data

## Table 66.9 — Pivotal Phase III Trials in Advanced Disease (1/2)

| Study | Regimen | No. of Patients | Locally Advanced No. (%) | Response Rate (%) | OS (mo) | P Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Burris et al. | Gemcitabine | 63 | NA | 5.4 | 5.65 | .0025 |
| | Bolus 5-FU | 63 | NA | 0 | 4.41 | |
| Moore et al. | Gemcitabine | 284 | 67 (25) | 8.0 | 5.91 | .038 |
| | Gemcitabine + erlotinib | 285 | 71 (24) | 8.6 | 6.24 | |
| Cunningham et al. | Gemcitabine | 266 | 76 (29) | 12.4 | 6.2 | .08 (meta-analysis = .02) |
| | Gemcitabine + capecitabine | 267 | 80 (30) | 19.1 | 7.1 | |

| Study | Regimen | No. of Patients | Response Rate (%) | OS (mo) | P Value |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Conroy et al. | Gemcitabine | 171 | 9.4 | 6.8 | < .001 |
| | Folinic acid + 5-FU + irinotecan + oxaliplatin (FOLFIRINOX) | 171 | 31.6 | 11.1 | |
| Von Hoff et al. | Gemcitabine | 430 | 7 | 6.7 | < .001 |
| | Gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel | 431 | 23 | 8.5 | |

## Key Takeaways — Adjuvant Chemoradiotherapy

- **GITSG/EORTC:** suggested benefit but small, flawed, underpowered
- **ESPAC-1:** **chemotherapy — not chemoradiation — drives survival benefit** (25% reduced death risk on meta-analysis)
- **RTOG 9704:** gemcitabine vs. 5-FU around CRT — no significant OS difference
- **EORTC 40013:** CRT reduces **local relapse** without OS benefit
- **Practice divide:** North America (selective CRT for high-risk) vs. Europe/Asia (chemotherapy alone standard)

## Key Takeaways — Adjuvant Chemotherapy

- **CONKO-001:** adjuvant gemcitabine improves DFS and long-term OS (10-yr: 12.2% vs. 7.7%)
- **ESPAC-3:** gemcitabine = 5-FU/FA efficacy with **better tolerability**; completing 6 cycles matters; delay up to 12 weeks is safe
- **JASPAC-01:** S-1 noninferior/superior in Japan (not approved in the West)
- **ESPAC-4:** GemCap — modest improvement; option for older/less fit patients
- **PRODIGE-24:** **mFOLFIRINOX standard for fit patients** (median OS 54.4 months)
- **APACT:** gem/nab-paclitaxel **investigational** pending mature OS

## Key Takeaways — Neoadjuvant Therapy

- Rationale: exponential growth, likely micrometastases at diagnosis, R1 rates
- **Resectability standardized** (consensus, MD Anderson, AHPBA/SSO/SSAT, NCCN; ISGPS-endorsed)
- **PREOPANC** (R0 72% vs. 43%; ITT OS benefit) and **JSAP-05** support neoadjuvant therapy
- **RECIST is inadequate** for response assessment after neoadjuvant therapy
- **A021806** will answer the definitive neoadjuvant vs. adjuvant question in North America

## Key Takeaways — Advanced/Palliative Disease

- 5-FU → **gemcitabine (1997)** → multi-agent era
- **GemCap** and **gem-erlotinib**: incremental gains
- **FOLFIRINOX (OS 11.1 mo)** and **gem/nab-paclitaxel (OS 8.5 mo)**: current standards for fit patients
- **JCOG1407:** prospective comparison maturing

## The Evolving Landscape

- **Patient selection** (CA19-9 limits), **supportive care**, and **therapy improvements** move the benchmark
- **Immune strategies:** personalized RNA vaccines, KRAS vaccines, checkpoint blockade combinations
- **MRD-guided treatment:** AMPLIFY (ELI-002 in ctDNA-positive, KRAS-mutant disease)
- **Germline-targeted approaches:** APOLLO — olaparib in BRCA1/BRCA2/PALB2-mutated resected disease
- **Total neoadjuvant strategies** under prospective evaluation (PREOPANC-2, A021806)

## Closing Summary

- Pancreatic cancer systemic therapy has advanced across the **entire disease continuum**:
  - **Adjuvant:** from 5-FU to mFOLFIRINOX (median OS > 54 months in fit patients)
  - **Neoadjuvant:** from concept to phase III evidence, with ongoing definitive trials
  - **Palliative:** doubling of median OS in the metastatic setting within two decades
- Future directions: **immunotherapy, MRD-guided and genotype-directed strategies, and refined perioperative sequencing**
